newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Key events in Zaire's rebel war.
newsitem.headline: Key events in Zaire's rebel war.

text.p: Here is a chronology of the conflict in Zaire, where rebels were reported on Saturday to have seized the airport of the country's third city, Kisangani:

Oct 7: Deputy governor of Zaire's South Kivu province tells 300,000-strong Banyamulenge community -- ethnic Tutsis settled in the region for generations -- to leave Zaire within a week or "be hunted down as rebels". Warning sparks a revolt.
Oct 24: Rebels seize their first major town, Uvira on northern shore of Lake Tanganyika.
Oct 30: Rebels capture Bukavu, capital of South Kivu province. Bukavu's Roman Catholic archbishop is among the dead.
Nov 1: Rebels and Rwandan soldiers capture Goma, main town in east; about 500 people killed in battles.
Nov 2: International aid workers flee Goma, leaving 1.1 million refugees in east Zaire without U.N. support or aid.
Nov 5: Eight African countries hold summit in Kenya; call for neutral military force to go to Zaire to help refugees.
Nov 9: Security Council asks United Nations to lay groundwork for a multinational force to help refugees.
Nov 14: Rebels bombard Mugunga, the biggest refugee camp, with rockets, mortars and heavy artillery for six hours.

Nov 15: Frightened Rwandan Hutu refugees surge out of Mugunga and other camps, head for home. Up to 700,000 return to Rwanda, rest flee west with armed Hutus blamed for 1994 genocide of minority Tutsis there.
Nov 24: Zaire marks 31 years of President Mobutu Sese Seko's rule; Mobutu is in Europe where he had been since cancer surgery in Switzerland in August.
Nov 28: Canadian commander of proposed U.N. force meets rebels, tours region; U.N.-backed military intervention idea fizzles out after exodus of refugees.
Dec 16: South African President Nelson Mandela and eight other African leaders meet in Kenya to discuss Central Africa crisis; Zaire shuns talks.
Dec 17: Mobutu flies home to a rousing reception; appoints new armed forces chief and reshuffles government to launch counter-offensive. He returns to France three weeks later.
Dec 25: Rebels say they took northeastern town of Bunia.
Jan 20: Government launches much-touted counter-offensive.
Jan 30: Rebels advance on several fronts, including mineral-rich Shaba Province; frustrate army counter-offensive.
Feb 5: Rebel leader Laurent Kabila gives Mobutu until Feb 21 to relinquish power or face all-out rebel offensive.
Feb 7: Mobutu returns to Zaire from Europe; U.N. refugee chief Sadako Ogata visits Zaire.
Feb 15: New U.N. and OAU special envoy for Central Africa Mohamed Sahnoun visits Zaire.
Feb 17: Zaire launches air strikes, bombing rebel-held towns of Bukavu, Shabunda and Walikale.
Feb 19: Mandela says South Africa tries to broker Zaire peace talks. Efforts fizzle out.
Feb 21: Mobutu leaves Zaire for France.
Feb 28: OAU foreign ministers urge Zaire ceasefire; call March 26 OAU summit in Togo on Central Africa crisis.
March 1: Aid workers leave Zaire's third city of Kisangani, citing insecurity and inability to work; rebels capture Lubutu to the south and abandoned refugee camp of Tingi Tingi.
March 3: Rebels capture Kindu; Zaire's main human rights group speaks of persistent reports of rebels massacring Hutus in east; rebels give army until March 13 to lay down weapons.
March 5: Zaire agrees to U.N. ceasefire plan; expels 11 U.N. aid workers.
March 7: U.N. Security Council calls on rebels to accept ceasefire plan; expresses concern at Hutu massacre reports.
March 8: Rebels say U.N. plan basis for talks; truce later.
March 13: Rebel deadline for Zairean soldiers to give up weapons passes with both sides preparing for showdown over eastern garrison city of Kisangani.
March 15: Rebels seize airport at Kisangani, diplomats and relief workers say.
